data.title: Reddit Fell While Profit Rose
data.description:

Investors who held Reddit over the past year are down 47.4%, including dividends. If you were weighing an investment back on 12 November 2025, which part of the original case for 33.6% revenue growth, a 28.4% profit margin and a 55.1x future P/E was most at risk of being too optimistic?

The Two Reddit Stories Investors Were Weighing

The shares cost US$203 at the start of the period, which left you choosing between two very different stories about where Reddit might be heading next.

On the optimistic side, one narrative saw expanding user content and global reach lifting the stock toward a fair value of US$219, built on assumptions of 33.6% revenue growth and a 28.4% profit margin.

The cautious view pointed to regulatory pressure on digital ads and moderation costs, with a fair value of US$129 and revenue growth assumptions limited to 24.6% and a 21.5% margin.

What The Results Changed In The Reddit Story

Reddit reported Q3 2026 revenue of US$894.957 million and net income of US$283.264 million, with net margin rising from 27.8% to 31.7% versus Q3 2025. That profitability level gave more support to the optimistic case that assumed a 28.4% margin, although slowing daily active user growth and search traffic concerns kept the cautious narrative alive. The evidence cut both ways.

The hinge assumption here was not user buzz, but sustained high margins. For another stock built on advertising or data licensing, focus on whether net income and margin progress line up with the original thesis rather than just tracking headline revenue.

What Reddit’s Drop Leaves You Paying For Today

Reddit now trades at US$99.55, with the one year return down 47.4%. The current bullish Narrative’s Fair Value sits above that price, based on business drivers rather than recent share moves.

According to rdiab, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, any buyer today is effectively judging whether Reddit’s community network effect can support durable monetisation as AI reshapes traffic patterns.

"Reddit’s moat is built on thousands of specialised communities, accumulated discussions, user reputations, moderation norms, voting systems, and network effects. A well-funded competitor or Google could replicate Reddit’s interface, but would struggle to recreate the trust, culture, relationships, moderation standards, and depth of content developed over many years."

That business sells ads, rents computing power and threads AI tools into everyday work software.

Advertisers choosing between Reddit and bigger players are really weighing niche engagement versus reach, data depth versus broad AI tooling.

If AI search and cloud spending keep absorbing budgets, the balance between community platforms and that broader ecosystem could matter more than any one quarter of Reddit headlines.

data.title: Andersons' (NASDAQ:ANDE) Profits May Not Reveal Underlying Issues
data.description:
The stock price didn't jump after The Andersons, Inc. (NASDAQ:ANDE) posted decent earnings last week. We did some digging and believe investors may be worried about some underlying factors in the report.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Andersons' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Andersons recorded an accrual ratio of 0.23. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, which is hardly a good thing. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of US$294m despite its profit of US$203.6m, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was US$234m a year ago though, so Andersons has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part. The good news for shareholders is that Andersons' accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

View our latest analysis for Andersons

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

Andersons' profit suffered from unusual items, which reduced profit by US$22m in the last twelve months. In the case where this was a non-cash charge it would have made it easier to have high cash conversion, so it's surprising that the accrual ratio tells a different story. It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. When we analysed the vast majority of listed companies worldwide, we found that significant unusual items are often not repeated. And that's hardly a surprise given these line items are considered unusual. If Andersons doesn't see those unusual expenses repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to increase over the coming year.

Our Take On Andersons' Profit Performance

In conclusion, Andersons' accrual ratio suggests that its statutory earnings are not backed by cash flow, even though unusual items weighed on profit. Given the contrasting considerations, we don't have a strong view as to whether Andersons's profits are an apt reflection of its underlying potential for profit. If you'd like to know more about Andersons as a business, it's important to be aware of any risks it's facing. data.title: What DNO Doubters Overlooked
data.description:
If DNO had sat on your watchlist instead of in your portfolio, the result might feel like a missed shot. Holding DNO over the past year would have returned 53.4%, including dividends. That kind of move naturally raises the question of what was visible back on 13 November 2025. Were the bold assumptions on record about North Sea expansion and higher future P/E already enough to flag that Sval Energi scale up as a potential turning point?

A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

DNO has already moved. See which of 195 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Two Stories DNO Investors Were Really Weighing

DNO shares cost NOK14.78 at the start of the period, which left you choosing between two very different stories about where the business might go next.

The bullish Narrative saw the Sval Energi deal and North Sea build out as the anchor. With a Fair Value of NOK17, it leaned on assumptions like 50.4% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 16.8% within three years.

The cautious view put more weight on political and energy transition risks. That bearish Narrative used a Fair Value of NOK12.5 and focused on threats like rising regulation, heavy Kurdistan exposure, and the possibility of higher decommissioning costs hurting future cash generation.

What The 2026 Evidence Did To The DNO Story

DNO’s Q3 2026 report showed revenue of US$1,023m and net income of US$90.3m, with net margin at 8.8% versus 1.7% a year earlier. That improvement in profitability, helped by record North Sea revenue and higher production, lined up more closely with the optimistic case that leaned on better margins, although the 16.8% target remained untested.

The key lesson is where to look. When a thesis leans on margin expansion like DNO’s bullish story did, track net income and net margin in each report and see whether they move toward the original forecast or stall.

What DNO's 53% Run Still Has You Paying For

DNO now trades at NOK21.12 after a 53.4% total return over the past year. The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St still places its Fair Value above that level, based on a view that the North Sea portfolio and a reshaped footprint can support stronger profitability over time.

The same Narrative argues today’s price does not yet fully credit the potential impact of fast track North Sea tiebacks and a maturing multi project discovery queue on future cash generation and earnings resilience.

"The nine project discovery portfolio that management is maturing for investment decisions through 2028, including fast track developments such as Kjøttkake, creates a pipeline of potential new tieback volumes that could sustain North Sea output and capital efficiency, supporting operating margins and cash flow."

Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the higher figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there

Looking Beyond DNO's Wells

DNO shows what can happen when producing assets and new fields align. You have seen how one producer story can hinge on volumes and margins.

Energy users still need someone to move molecules, not just pull them from the ground. That is where another business focuses its effort.

It builds and runs long haul pipes, storage caverns and utility networks for oil, gas and some renewables. Those assets earn mainly through fees rather than commodity bets.

As demand for transport, storage and distribution shifts, the role of these regulated and contracted systems could change. That is the adjacent story worth keeping in view next to DNO.
